::: {#exm-hers-partial-f}
#### Partial F-test of age and exercise in HERS

For the models of @exm-hers-nested-models,
`anova()` gives the [partial F-test](#def-partial-f-test):

```{r}
#| label: hers-partial-f-anova
#| code-fold: false
anova(fit_smaller, fit_larger) |>
  parameters::parameters() |>
  parameters::print_md(digits = 3, footer = "")
```

The definition gives the same [statistic](sufficiency.qmd#def-statistic):

```{r}
#| label: hers-partial-f-by-hand
#| code-fold: false
rss0 <- sum(residuals(fit_smaller)^2)
rss1 <- sum(residuals(fit_larger)^2)
n <- nobs(fit_larger)
p <- length(coef(fit_larger)) - 1
q <- p - (length(coef(fit_smaller)) - 1)
f_stat <- ((rss0 - rss1) / q) / (rss1 / (n - p - 1))
c(
  f = f_stat,
  p_value = pf(f_stat, q, n - p - 1, lower.tail = FALSE)
)
```

With $q = `r q`$ and $n - p - 1 = `r n - p - 1`$,
$F = `r round(f_stat, 2)`$,
so the data `r if (pf(f_stat, q, n - p - 1, lower.tail = FALSE) < 0.05) "reject" else "do not reject"`
$H_0$ at the 5% level.
:::
